summary: During the Battle of Yamaamah, Thaabit bin Qais and Saalim dug a foxhole, refused to flee and fought until they were martyred.

people.name: Muhammad bin Thaabit bin Qais bin Shammaas

notes: Two reports joined: an unnamed daughter of Thaabit, then Muhammad bin Thaabit. Saalim's words appear in both.

summary: Abbaad bin Bishr told Abu Sa'eed Khudri of his dream of martyrdom, then led four hundred Ansaar in the attack at Yamaamah and was martyred.
At Yamaamah, the mortally wounded Abu Aqeel answered Ma'n bin Adi's call to the Ansaar, fought, and died after learning that Musaylama had been killed.

people.name: Ja'far bin Abdullaah bin Aslam Hamdaani

summary: Before the Battle of Yamaamah, Thaabit bin Qais perfumed himself for battle, refused to join the flight and was killed fighting.
At Yamaamah, Thaabit bin Qais cursed the enemy and the retreating Muslims, killed a man standing on a wall and was martyred.
notes: Narrator not named in the text.

summary: At the Battle of Yarmook, Ikrama bin Abu Jahal dismounted and walked into the fighting against Khaalid bin Waleed's advice, and was martyred.
At Yarmook, Ikrama bin Abu Jahal and about four hundred Muslims pledged to fight to the death in front of Khaalid's tent, and many of them, including Diraar, were martyred.
notes: Text spells the Companion Diraar bin Azwar; matched to the approved diraar-bin-azoor. The narrator may be the approved abu-uthmaan entry, but that is not confirmed, so tagged as a new person.

summary: After Yarmook, Khaalid bin Waleed tended the badly wounded Ikrama and his son Amr, and said that Allaah had blessed the Muslims with martyrs although Umar had said they would not be martyred.
notes: Unnamed narrator ('another narration').

summary: At Siffeen, Ammaar bin Yaasir asked Ali why he had not yet been martyred, drank the milk he had been told would be his last drink, and fought until he was martyred.
Abu Sinaan Duwali saw Ammaar bin Yaasir ask for milk, drink it, and say he would soon meet the Prophet and his companions.
notes: Ends with 'The rest of the Hadith follows'.

summary: At Siffeen, Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan heard Ammaar bin Yaasir say he would meet Allaah and the damsels of Jannah, and recalled the Prophet's words that the milk would be his last provision.

people.name: Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf

summary: Anas describes his brother Baraa bin Maalik's courage, and how Baraa led a counter-attack in Persia after the Muslims retreated and was martyred there.
notes: Two reports joined: Anas's account, then an unnamed 'another narration'.

summary: Umar bin Khattaab said he had thought less of Uthmaan bin Madh'oon for dying a natural death, until he realised that even the best of people die naturally.
notes: The text gives him (RA); he is generally known as a Taabi'i, so the sahabi flag follows the text and should be checked.

summary: Ali said that Abu Bakr was the bravest of people, having stood guard over the Prophet with a drawn sword during the Battle of Badr.
Ali said that Umar bin Khattaab alone made Hijrah openly, with sword on his neck and bow on his shoulder, daring the Quraysh to stop him.
After Uhud, Ali asked Faatima to take his sword and recited verses; the Prophet praised Sahal bin Hunayf, Abu Dujaana and Ibn Simma for their fighting, and Jibra'eel said Ali was from him.
notes: Two reports joined: Jaabir's, and Abdullaah bin Abbaas's. Jibra'eel is an angel and is left out of people. The third Sahabi whose name a narrator forgot is not named.

summary: During the Battle of Khandaq, Ali killed Amr bin Abd Wadd in single combat after Amr's challenge.
Amr bin Abd Wadd challenged the Muslims three times; Ali accepted despite the Prophet's caution, and after a fierce exchange killed him.
notes: Ali's lineage is given as 'the son of Abu Taalib'; Abd Manaaf in Amr's question is an ancestor and is left out.

summary: After killing Amr bin Abd Wadd, Ali recited verses, returned to the Prophet, and explained to Umar why he had not taken Amr's armour.
notes: Continues the duel account from n00698; the opening verses are Ali's speech after the fight.

summary: Salama bin Akwa tells of the Khaybar expedition, where Aamir was killed in a fall of his own sword, and of Marhab coming out with a challenge.
notes: Ends mid-challenge; Marhab's challenge and Aamir's reply continue in n00701.

summary: Aamir accidentally wounded himself fatally with his own sword in his duel with Marhab; the Prophet gave the flag to Ali, cured his eyes with saliva, and Ali killed Marhab.
notes: Continues from n00700 mid-poem.

summary: Abu Raafi, in Ali's party at Khaybar, describes Ali tearing a fortress door off to use as a shield, a door that a group of eight could not turn over afterwards.
Jaabir reports that Ali lifted a fortress door at Khaybar so the Muslims could climb the walls, and that later forty men could not lift it back.
Three reports: Ali lifted the Khaybar door, Jaabir bin Samura gave a variant of it, and Talha recited verses at Uhud praising Zubayr's sword and defending the Prophet.
notes: Three reports joined: an unnamed narrator, Jaabir bin Samura, and Talha's verses. The 'Ghaalib and Maalik tribes' are not people.

summary: Urwa reports that as a boy of twelve, Zubayr heard a rumour that the Prophet had been captured, drew his sword and went to find him in Makkah; the Prophet prayed for him and his sword.
notes: Text gives 'Hadhrat Urwa (RA)', matched to the unsure entry urwa-bin-zubayr; the vocab also has urwa (unsure) and urwa-bin-masood (yes), which were not used.

summary: At Uhud, Zubayr accepted Talha Abdari's challenge, leapt onto his camel, killed him with his own sword, and was praised by the Prophet.
notes: Not the Companion Talha bin Ubaydillaah (vocab id talha).

summary: During the Battle of Khandaq, Zubayr answered Naufal Makhzoomi's challenge and split him in two with one blow, then returned reciting verses that defend the Nabi.

people.name: Naufal bin Abdullaah bin Mughiera Makhzoomi

summary: Asmaa bint Abu Bakr reports that at the Prophet's word Zubayr took on a mushrik who had challenged from a height, and killed him after he fell into the ditch.
At Khandaq, Abdullaah bin Zubayr, a boy kept with the women and children in a fortress, describes watching his father Zubayr fight, and his father's reply.
notes: Umar bin Abu Salama is not the approved umar (Umar bin Khattaab) and not abu-salma.

summary: At Yarmook, Zubayr broke through the enemy alone, was wounded on both sides of his old Badr wound, and left his ten-year-old son Abdullaah in the care of a companion.
notes: Narrator matched to urwa-bin-zubayr as in n00705.

summary: When the Sahabah asked Zubayr a second time to lead an attack, he complied as he had the first time.
notes: Fragment of the Yarmook account in n00710; the request itself is described there. The footnote citation at the end is left out of the tags.

summary: At Raabigh, Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas defended the Muslims with arrows and was the first to shoot an arrow in the path of Allaah, recalling it in verse.
Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas killed three men with one returned arrow at Uhud, and at Badr fought as effectively as a cavalryman while on foot.
notes: Two reports joined: Ibn Shihaab (Uhud) and Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (Badr).

summary: Hamza bin Abdil Muttalib wore ostrich feathers at Badr, and the Mushrikeen said he had carried out all the major offensives against them.
Umayyah bin Khalaf asked Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf who had marked himself with ostrich feathers at Badr, and on hearing it was Hamza, said Hamza had carried out all the major offensives against them.
After Uhud, the Prophet searched for Hamza, wept over his mutilated body, had a cloth laid over it, and declared him the leader of the martyrs on the Day of Qiyaamah.
Wahshi tells how he killed Hamza at Uhud to win his freedom, later came to the Prophet in Madinah to accept Islaam, and at Yamaamah killed Musaylama with the same spear.

people.name: Ja'far bin Amr bin Umayyah Dhamri

notes: Ja'far bin Amr is not the approved amr-bin-umayyah-dhamri (Amr bin Umayyah Dhamri).

summary: A variant report of Wahshi's account: Sibaa stepped forward to challenge the Muslims, and Hamza answered and killed him.

people.name: Ja'far bin Amr bin Umayyah Dhamri

notes: Variant of n00717. The lineage phrase 'son of Ummu Anmaar' is left out, and the Bukhari citation is treated as a reference.

summary: At Taa'if, Handhala bin Rabee was captured by the people of Taa'if, and Abbaas bin Abdil Muttalib, answering the Prophet's call, snatched him back despite a barrage of stones.
At Badr, two young Ansaar asked Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf to point out Abu Jahal, killed him, and the Prophet gave his possessions to Mu'aadh bin Amr bin Jamooh, whose arm had been cut off in the fight.
notes: Several reports joined: Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf's account with a variant, then Mu'aadh bin Amr's own account via Abdullaah bin Abbaas and Abdullaah bin Abi Bakr. The Bukhari citation is treated as a reference.
